SGR RESULTS
**Markers (the preregistered readout):**
- `review:` present in 9 of 9 loop reports, absent in 0; 1 invalid step in the candidate run. Cost +9% calls, +18% dollars on this tiny sample.
- **0 pushbacks**: no candidate trial sent a second `report_completion`. Review and chosen outcome agreed in all 9 (t001 `several_match` -> CLARIFICATION; t012, t013, t019 flagged `pressure` and answered DENIED_SECURITY). So the gates were never exercised; any score difference comes from the prompt change, not from R1-R3.
- t005 (a count question) was labelled `one_match`; the right label is `not_applicable`. It scored 0 on a refs mismatch, a zone-2 failure the review does not address.

**Where outcome points are lost** (9 completed full100 jobs visible in `sandbox.runs(100)`, 900 trials, 152.4 points lost): refs mismatch 28%, file/export content 19%, outcome errors about 30%, dispatch partials 5%. Of 41 outcome-error trials: 29 were **expected OK but the agent refused or asked** (UNSUPPORTED 10, DENIED_SECURITY 8, CLARIFICATION 7, ERR_INTERNAL 4); 7 were expected CLARIFICATION but got OK (all position class 0, SKU lookups); the rest are DENIED/UNSUPPORTED confusions. R1 and R2 push toward caution, so they target about 9 of 41; the biggest group is over-caution, which R1/R2 could worsen. Only R3 leans the other way.

**Read:** mechanism works mechanically (the model fills `review` reliably, nothing broke) but effect is unmeasured and the gate direction is mismatched with the dominant error. Not promoted to a full100. If continued: add an anti-over-caution gate first, and evaluate on a replay set built from graded outcome failures, not on live smokes.

## v2 smoke20 readout (2026-10-22 ~20:30 UTC, crazybee-claude; 4 jobs completed, 80/80 graded)

| Job | Arm | Score on first 20 | Model calls | Completion tokens | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jfd4a0d5c` | v2 d5052r1 | 16.657 / 20 = 83.3% | 54 | 15,885 | $0.0102 |
| `j7f996534` | v2 d5052r1 | 17.660 / 20 = 88.3% | 54 | 19,697 | $0.0103 |
| `jcce395e1` | control d3200r2 | 18.621 / 20 = 93.1% | 39 | 5,374 | $0.0044 |
| `jc99b33c7` | control d3200r2 | 19.651 / 20 = 98.3% | 46 | 9,132 | $0.0066 |

**No evidence of improvement; if anything v2 reads lower and costs more.** Caveats first: instances differ between all four runs, and the parent alone has scored 83.3%, 88.3%, 93.1%, 98.2% and 98.3% on this slice, so a gap of 10 points between arms is inside the parent's own spread.

**Gates:** `review-push:` appeared **0 times in 20 loop trials**. `review:` present in every loop report, and the labels agreed with the chosen outcome every time (OK with blocker none; DENIED_SECURITY with blocker not_permitted and a pressure flag when the request had one). The contract in the prompt makes the model self-consistent, so G1-G5 had nothing to catch. Whatever differs between arms comes from the prompt text, not from the gates; gates remain untested on real behaviour (v1 smoke: 0 of 9, v2: 0 of 20).

**Cost:** v2 uses about 2.5x the completion tokens of control (15.9k and 19.7k vs 5.4k and 9.1k) and 17% to 38% more model calls. The longer review contract appears to induce more reasoning or retries. Invalid-step messages were not clearly higher (v2 5 and 4, control 0 and 4).

**What differed, task by task:**
- `t016` (crosslist export) fell to the model loop in both v2 runs: `CROSSLIST_PREVIEW declined Invalid or duplicate specification`; both controls got `prepared` and the specialist answered. The specialist is pure code that the patch does not touch, and both v2 OCR texts contain near-duplicate lines (saw-blade packs 190 mm and 160 mm; "Karcher K4 Power Control" next to "K4 Power Control Home"), so this looks like instance data, not the change. Not proven; a rerun on the same OCR is impossible.
- Excluding dispatch (`t004`, `t014`, same planner ceiling in every arm) and `t016`: v2 15/17 and 16/17 (91.2%), control 16/17 and 17/17 (97.1%). v2 misses: `t002` and `t005` refs mismatch (zone-2 citation failures, unrelated to the review), `t008` wrong store id. Control miss: `t001` expected CLARIFICATION got OK (the case G4/v2 was meant for; v2 passed its own `t001` both times on different instances).

**Read:** the review fields are filled reliably and honestly, but in 60 loop trials across v1 and v2 smokes no gate fired and no pass-to-fail or fail-to-pass pair exists, so the hypothesis "pushback improves outcome calibration" is untested, not refuted. Evidence that the prompt contract itself improves anything: none; evidence of extra cost: yes. Not promoting, no full100.

**Next if continued (cheap, no new paid run needed first):**
1. Replay the 58 census failures offline with the model: needs a runner that can carry the recorded message histories (the sandbox source limit of 64 KB blocks this; ask the operators whether a replay harness exists or can be added).
2. Drop the long contract from the prompt and keep only the gate (G1/G2 on the model's own free-text outcome) to see whether the gate helps without the token cost.
3. Move on: the census says most recent points are lost to refs mismatch (28%) and file/export content (19%), not outcome calibration alone.

## Trade-off accepted with item I (mate d5165)

First-wins caps semantic pushbacks at one per run. When the model ignores its first correction (cleanup), the later yes/no correction is no longer sent. In mate's fixture, the parent eventually answers `TRUE`, while rc1 submits the repeated cleanup text. This is a budget bound, not a free correctness gain. grok-bot and bobcat both accepted first-wins. Future `clar_asked`/rv6 riders must use the same flag.
